    15  # Chebyshev polynomials over the reals: some extremal properties
    16  
    17  * Chebyshev polynomials have largest leading coefficient,
    18  following proof in https://math.stackexchange.com/a/978145/1277
    19  * Chebyshev polynomials maximize iterated derivatives at 1 and beyond
    20  
    21  ## Main statements
    22  
    23  * leadingCoeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one: If `P` is a real polynomial of degree at most `n` and
    24    `|P (x)| ≤ 1` for all `x ∈ [-1, 1]` then the leading coefficient of `P` is at most `2 ^ (n - 1)`
    25  * leadingCoeff_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one: When `n ≥ 2`, equality holds iff `P = T_n`
    26  * eval_iterate_derivative_le_of_forall_abs_le_one: If `P` is a real polynomial of degree at most `n`
    27    and `|P (x)| ≤ 1` for all `x ∈ [-1, 1]` then for all `x ≥ 1`, `P ^ (k) (x) ≤ T_n ^ (k)(x)`
    28  * eval_iterate_derivative_eq_iff_of_forall_abs_le_one: If `0 < k ≤ n` then equality holds iff
    29    `P = T_n`

    31  ## Implementation

    33  We describe the proof for the leading coefficient; the proof for iterated derivatives uses a
    34  similar approach.
    35  
    36  By monotonicity of `2 ^ (n - 1)`, we can assume that `P` has degree exactly `n`.
    37  Using Lagrange interpolation, we can give a formula for the leading coefficient of `P`
    38  as a linear combination of the values of `P` on the Chebyshev nodes (sumNodes_eq_coeff).

    40  coefficients of the linear combination (negOnePow_mul_leadingCoeffC_pos).
    41  Since `|P (x)| ≤ 1` on the nodes, this implies that the leading coefficient of `P` is bounded
    42  by that of `T_n`, which is known to equal `2 ^ (n - 1)`.
    43  Moreover, equality holds iff `P` and `T_n` agree on the nodes, which implies that they coincide.

   311        rw [(eval_T_real_eq_one_iff hn _).mpr ⟨0, by simp, by simp⟩] at this
   312        assumption
   313    · rintro ⟨k, hk, hx⟩
   314      rw [hx]

   317  theorem irrational_of_isRoot_T_real {n : ℕ} {x : ℝ} (hroot : (T ℝ n).IsRoot x) (hnz : x ≠ 0) :
   318      Irrational x := by
   319    rw [← mem_roots (T_ne_zero ℝ n), roots_T_real, Finset.mem_val] at hroot
   320    obtain ⟨k, hk₁, hk₂⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hroot
   321    have hn : n ≠ 0 := by grind
   322    suffices Irrational (cos ((Rat.divInt (2 * k + 1) (2 * n)) * π)) by
   323      rw [← hk₂]; convert! this using 2; push_cast; field_simp
   324    apply irrational_cos_rat_mul_pi
   325    contrapose! hnz
   326    have : (Rat.divInt (2 * k + 1) (2 * n)).den = 2 * (n / n.gcd (2 * k + 1)) := calc
   327      _ = 2 * n / (2 * n).gcd (2 * k + 1) := by rw [Rat.den_divInt]; norm_cast; simp [hn]
   328      _ = _ := by rw [Nat.Coprime.gcd_mul_left_cancel n (by simp),
   329        Nat.mul_div_assoc _ (Nat.gcd_dvd_left ..)]
   330    have hn : 2 * k + 1 = n := Nat.eq_of_dvd_of_lt_two_mul (by simp) (Nat.gcd_eq_left_iff_dvd.mp <|
   331      Nat.eq_of_dvd_of_div_eq_one (Nat.gcd_dvd_left ..) (by grind [Rat.den_pos])) (by grind)
   332    rw_mod_cast [← hk₂, hn]; convert! cos_pi_div_two using 2; push_cast; field_simp

   334  theorem abs_iterate_derivative_T_real_le (n : ℤ) (k : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : |x| ≤ 1) :
   335      |(derivative^[k] (T ℝ n)).eval x| ≤ (derivative^[k] (T ℝ n)).eval 1 := by
   336    wlog hn : 0 ≤ n
   337    · convert! this (-n) k hx (by grind) using 1 <;> rw [T_neg]
   338    lift n to ℕ using hn
   339    have := T_iterate_derivative_mem_span_T (R := ℝ) n k
   340    obtain ⟨f, hfsupp, hfderiv⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_set.mp this
   341    replace hfderiv : ∑ p ∈ f.support, f p • p = derivative^[k] (T ℝ n) := by rw [← hfderiv]; rfl
   342    have hf (y : ℝ) :
   343        ∑ p ∈ f.support, f p • p.eval y = (derivative^[k] (T ℝ n)).eval y := by
   344      rw [← hfderiv, Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
   345      simp_rw [Polynomial.eval_smul]
   346    rw [← hf x, ← hf 1]
   347    grw [Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs]
   348    refine Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i hi => ?_)
   349    obtain ⟨m, hm, hi⟩ := (Set.mem_image ..).mp (hfsupp hi)
   350    grw [abs_nsmul, ← hi, abs_eval_T_real_le_one m hx]
   351    simp
